microgravity-cpr.source: Hinkelbein J, et al. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) during spaceflight - a guideline for CPR in microgravity from the German Society of Aerospace Medicine (DGLRM) and the European Society of Aerospace Medicine Space Medicine Group (ESAM-SMG). Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med. 2020;28:108. doi:10.1186/s13049-020-00793-y

spacecraft-transit.basis: Aims and scope of the guideline: CPR in microgravity

notes.text: During space exploration missions to Mars, telemedicine support will be impractical during CPR because of the communication time delay (3 to 23 min), and should only be attempted when additional crewmembers, not involved in treating the patient, are present.

station.basis: Aims and scope of the guideline: CPR in microgravity

notes.text: In low Earth orbit, telemedicine support should be consulted in a cardiac arrest when it seems feasible and enough crew are available.
The guideline covers microgravity only. It mentions that other techniques have been suggested for hypogravity, but it makes no recommendation for partial gravity.
